utterances.text: Now, you said you saw him going into the retirement home. When you saw him, were you and the others lined up awaiting for your morning assignments?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the defendant Blagoje Simic, did you see him in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him once in front of the home of -- retirement home, and once just when he was passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And those were the only two times that you saw him between April and December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw him going into the retirement home, were you and the others assembled there waiting for your work assignments?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we weren't all there, because some groups already had left. I was standing a bit longer in front of the retirement home because the truck didn't arrive yet. On that occasion, the truck didn't arrive yet. But there were also occasionally other reasons why we didn't go immediately after arriving at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: However, on that occasion, were you alone waiting for your assignment, or were there others with you waiting for an assignment when you saw Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: There were also other people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, Milan Simic, do you know Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And during the period of April to December while you were forced to work, did you see Milan Simic as you moved throughout the area?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Only one, when passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So will only on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to talk about some other situations or incidents that occurred during that period while you were working. Were your parents alive? Were your parents living in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where was your mother living?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: My mother lived in Tito's Street in an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, where did she keep her valuables?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: She worked as a salesperson in a kiosk selling cigarettes. She wasn't well off. But whatever she had, she kept in her handbag. She had a few hundred Marks, and some gold. She kept that in her handbag.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And she kept that in her handbag as opposed to using a bank?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how old was your mother in 1992, in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: My mother was born in 1927. She was born in 1927.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know what month, sir?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So she was approximately 65 years old. And did something happen to her in April of 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. She encountered an orthodox priest, Prota [as interpreted] -- Tota, she asked where are you going? To see my children. He pushed her, and took her bag. Tota.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is definitely some sort of mistake in the transcript. Page 86, line 2, she encountered an orthodox priest, Prota, and I really don't believe this is what the witness stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's a problem in translation. I'll fix it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can you correct it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was just waiting for him to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir,, we seem to have a bit of a problem with the translation here. Who did your mother encounter in April of 1992 that took her handbag?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Tota.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you say "Tota" are you referring to Nuzim Ramusovic?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The same person who was shot, lying in the street, about a month earlier?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The person who you did not speak highly of?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he was not an orthodox priest, for the record?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were there other thefts? I'd like to talk to you about other thefts that were happening in Bosanski Samac beginning in April. Were there thefts of vehicles that were occurring in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who was taking vehicles, or stealing vehicles, in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: The vehicles in Bosanski Samac, some were stolen by the 4th Detachment, and others by others who were coming from outside. Outsiders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say --

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you say "Serbian outsiders," do you mean the paramilitary soldiers?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: All these were paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, people of what ethnic group lost their vehicles?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Muslims and Catholics. But I'm aware of three examples, three cases, of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you have any relatives, first? Any of your relatives have their vehicles stolen or robbed from them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: My brother-in-law, Sead Krajtin [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what happened? Tell the Court what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a certain person came to his home, Crni, with two other people. He asked for his registration of automobile, the automobile documents, the driver's licence, and they left and took the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was your brother-in-law given a receipt or any document indicating that his car was being seized?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about your neighbours? Did any of your neighbours have a car taken from them?

utterances.speaker: NUSRET HADZIJUSUFOVIC
utterances.text: When the mosque was demolished, I was checking in my roof. Then I was looking at Omeragic's place, my neighbours. Nenad Bijelic came to him, Smudj's son, and another two, Cabasko, and other two people who I didn't know. They were all in uniform. They forced him to open his garage, drove out the car, and left. Later, I was looking at that, seeing that with my very eyes. He told me later on that they just said this is for the needs of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, is it time to break now? It's just about 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. How much time do you still need, Mr. Weiner, to complete the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sometime tomorrow afternoon. We'll be completed sometime tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I said how much time? An hour? Because we don't seem we will go through this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would say one to two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, allow me to address another issue which is not related to this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In that case, we will release the witness. Witness, you are released for now. You should come back tomorrow to complete the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be very brief, Your Honours. I kindly ask this Honourable Trial Chamber to consider the possibility with regard to the Christian Orthodox Easter which is on the 5th of May, to adjust our sitting days and hours, and I raise this issue on behalf of four clients and all of my colleagues. It is on the 5th of May. Since we are starting to sit from the 1st of May, and the Good Friday would be on the 3rd of May, and Easter Monday is on the 6th May, I would like to ask the appropriate ruling of this Trial Chamber, especially given the fact that the Croatian detainees here of Catholic religion and the Muslim detainees of Muslim religion were to some sort granted to respect their religious holidays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking for the ruling now or your answer. But just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, we may give you an answer later. What I want to say is that these religious holidays which we observe in the Tribunal are actually UN holidays adopted by the United Nations. That is why we observe them. There are other religious holidays that we don't observe in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But this is a specific institution, UN institution, dealing with the three ethnic groups from Balkans, from former Yugoslavia. I absolutely understand the policy of United Nations with regard to the -- well, certain religious holidays. But now we are here dealing with really specific, I would say, backgrounds, traditions, personal moments, et cetera. And also, I can add that in some other trials, the Trial Chamber will not sit on this week prior to -- I mean, just a couple of days prior to Easter, if this fact is of any assistance to your possible decision. Not to mention that we can, Your Honours, maybe in coming months, maybe to adjust these two days to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. some extent. I mean, not to be in delay. I understand. I am perfectly aware about the specific situation in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. My other comment would be if you wanted them to be UN holidays, then that is up to the states concerned to take the matter up with the relevant organs of the United Nations. Any comments from the Prosecution? MR. Di FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I think the position of the Prosecution is that it remains neutral in this issue. I can well understand the Chamber's concern about keeping the trial moving and the fact that they are not UN holidays. On the other hand, it is one of the more important occurrences in the Christian calendar, and I can understand the concern of the defendants and Defence counsel. So I think it is best that the Prosecution just remain neutral on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber will consider the matter and issue a decision within this week. The proceedings will adjourn and continue tomorrow in the afternoon at 14.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
